title: Normative Modeling of Amygdala Subfields and Disease-Specific Vulnerabilities Across Neurological Disorders.
abstract: As an integrative center of the limbic system, the amygdala and its subfields participate in diverse neural functions and demonstrate heterogeneous structural changes in various neurological disorders. In this study, three-dimensional T1-weighted MRI data from 22,258 healthy participants were analyzed using normative modeling to establish normative references for the volumes of the amygdala and its subfields. These models elucidated the developmental and aging curves of the amygdala and identified distinct ages at peak volume across subfields, ranging from 24.6 to 43.7 years. Based on these references, individual centile scores were calculated for 4132 patients with mild cognitive impairment, Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, cerebral small vessel disease, multiple sclerosis, and neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder. These centile scores not only captured disease-specific deviation patterns of the amygdala subfields but also demonstrated utility in disease classification. Moreover, the centile scores correlated with clinical measures of cognitive function, emotional state, and motor performance across disorders. These findings suggest that normative references of the amygdala subfields provide insights into cross-disease alteration patterns and offer potential neuroimaging biomarkers to aid differential diagnosis and clinical assessment.

title: Liquid Chromatography/tandem Mass Spectrometry-based Target Engagement of Lysine-specific Demethylase 1 Inhibitor TAK-418 Through Detecting Covalent Adducts in the Brain.
abstract: Translating pharmacokinetics (PK) and pharmacodynamics (PD) from preclinical to clinical is important in successful development of drugs for central nervous system (CNS) diseases. TAK-418 is a clinical candidate of lysine-specific demethylase 1 (LSD1) inhibitor with a unique mechanism of action; it covalently binds to flavin adenine dinucleotide (FAD) to form a compact adduct formylated FAD (F-FAD), thereby minimizing hematological side effect risks. In this study, we established a liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC/MS/MS)-based approach for evaluating F-FAD as a target engagement marker for TAK-418 to advance PK/PD translation and clinical dose setting. In rats, LC/MS/MS enabled detection of TAK-418-induced F-FAD formation in the brain with chromatographic separation from native FAD. F-FAD levels were positively associated with LSD1 protein abundance across brain regions and increased with increasing TAK-418 dose. LSD1 occupancy calculated from F-FAD concentrations was correlated with the inhibition level of LSD1 enzyme activity in rat hippocampus. This mechanism-based approach provides a link between covalent adduct formation, target engagement, and enzyme inhibition in the brain. In addition, similar point estimates of the half-maximal effective concentration (EC50)​ for F-FAD formation in rat and human hippocampal homogenates support the potential utility of F-FAD measurements for translational assessment of LSD1 target engagement. These findings provide useful information for evaluating the translational relationship between TAK-418 exposure and LSD1 target engagement and may support future PK/PD modeling and clinical dose selection for TAK-418. Moreover, our methodology for measuring covalent adducts would be applicable for multiple CNS drug candidates with covalent binding property.

title: Combined rituximab and magnesium acetyl taurate therapy attenuates neurodegeneration via ERK/c-JNK/P38MAPK signaling modulation in methylmercury-induced amyotrophic lateral sclerosis-like neurotoxicity.
abstract: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by motor neuron degeneration, oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, mitochondrial dysfunction, and dysregulation of intracellular signaling pathways. The present study investigated the neuroprotective potential of rituximab (RTXMB), alone and in combination with magnesium acetyl taurate (MACT600), against methylmercury (MLMC5)-induced ALS-like pathology in adult Wistar rats through modulation of the ERK/c-JNK/P38MAPK signaling pathway. ALS was induced by oral administration of MLMC5 (5 mg/kg) for 21 days. RTXMB (50 and 100 mg/kg) and MACT600 (600 mg/kg) treatments were administered from day 22 to day 42. Behavioral assessments, neurochemical estimations, ELISA, Western blotting, hematological analysis, gross morphology, and histopathological evaluations were performed. MLMC5 exposure produced significant impairments in locomotion, muscular strength, cognition, and emotional behavior, accompanied by increased oxidative stress, inflammatory cytokines, glutamate excitotoxicity, apoptotic markers, methylmercury accumulation, and dysregulation of ERK/c-JNK/P38MAPK signaling. Moreover, MLMC5 caused marked demyelination, neuronal degeneration, neurotransmitter imbalance, skeletal muscle damage, and hematological dysfunction. RTXMB treatment significantly attenuated these pathological alterations in a dose-dependent manner, with RTXMB100 showing greater neuroprotective efficacy. Combined administration of RTXMB100 and MACT600 demonstrated the most pronounced therapeutic effects by restoring antioxidant defenses, suppressing neuroinflammation and apoptosis, normalizing neurotransmitter levels, preserving myelin integrity, and improving neuronal morphology. The findings suggest that RTXMB, particularly in combination with MACT600, exerts potent neuroprotective effects against ALS-like pathology via modulation of MAPK signaling pathways and may represent a promising therapeutic strategy for ALS management.

title: Micronuclear ecDNA constrains tumor cell fitness and is associated with favorable patient survival.
abstract: Extrachromosomal DNA (ecDNA) contributes to cancer genome instability by enabling high-copy oncogene amplification and genetic intratumoral heterogeneity. Micronuclei (MNs) are common in chromosomally unstable cancers, yet their role in ecDNA-driven tumors remains unclear. Here we investigate how ecDNA damage, mitotic segregation and MN formation are linked. We find that ecDNAs are a major source of MNs following their damage, particularly under replication stress. Replication stress promotes mitotic ecDNA clustering, asymmetric inheritance, mis-segregation into MNs and reduced transcriptional output. Single-MN sequencing reveals that multiple distinct ecDNA species coalesce within individual MNs. Cells inheriting ecDNA+ MNs display impaired proliferative capacity and are more likely to undergo cell death. In patients with MYCN-amplified neuroblastoma, higher frequencies of ecDNA+ MNs at diagnosis are associated with improved overall survival. Together, these findings identify ecDNA mis-segregation as a mechanism that limits tumor fitness, highlighting mitotic ecDNA retention as a potential therapeutic vulnerability.

title: Acute Ultra Low Dose THC Attenuates Anxiety-Like Behavior in a Mouse Model for Major-Depressive Disorder.
abstract: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is a prevalent psychiatric disorder, and is a leading cause of disability worldwide. Current treatments for MDD entail many side effects, and include a lag until the onset of therapeutic effects. The current hypotheses as for the etiology of MDD revolve around the monoamine hypothesis and the plasticity and neurodegeneration hypothesis. According to the latter, employing a neuroprotective treatment may help ameliorate depressive symptoms. Δ9-Tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) is the primary psychoactive component of the cannabis sativa plant. THC interacts with the endocannabinoid system, which was shown to be involved in the regulation of emotional states (e.g. anxiety) and stress through modulation of synaptic plasticity. Here, we show the potential of acute, ultra-low dose (0.002 mg/kg) THC in ameliorating anxious behavior in a chronic mild stress mouse model for MDD. We utilize next generation sequencing techniques to show the treatment's effect on neuronal differentiation and synaptic plasticity-related mRNAs, and specify Elmo domain containing 1 (Elmod1) as a molecular mediator of the observed anxiolytic effects. Moreover, we show the involvement of glucocorticoids-related mRNAs in the observed anxiolytic effect of acute, ultra-low dose THC.

title: Beyond reconstruction: minimally invasive aesthetic and regenerative medicine in postoperative oral and maxillofacial surgery.
abstract: Oral and maxillofacial reconstruction restores anatomical continuity and function after tumor resection, trauma and congenital deformity, yet patients frequently remain affected by fibrosis, scar tethering, impaired oral competence, asymmetry and altered dynamic facial function. These deficits can impair quality of life, social interaction and body image. Conventional revision surgery carries additional morbidity, and minimally invasive options have emerged as a postoperative adjunct. This article reviews how minimally invasive aesthetic and regenerative medicine can extend reconstructive rehabilitation in oral and maxillofacial surgery. Current biological and clinical evidence for polynucleotides (PN), hyaluronic acid (HA) and botulinum toxin A (BoNT-A) was reviewed and integrated with selected, non-consecutive illustrative cases from a dedicated aesthetic and regenerative consultation in an academic oral and maxillofacial surgery department. Clinical applications were illustrated across four patient categories: oncological, congenital, trauma/scar and aesthetic-functional sequelae after surgery. In illustrative cases from different categories, a staged approach of tissue conditioning, structural restoration and dynamic neuromodulation was associated with clinically observed and patient-reported improvements in scar pliability, tissue gliding, oral competence, dynamic symmetry and quality of life. PN were used primarily for regenerative tissue conditioning, HA for reversible structural restoration, and BoNT-A to modulate muscular imbalance and pathological wound tension. As interventions were frequently combined and no validated outcome measures or controls were used, these observations are hypothesis-generating. Minimally invasive regenerative and aesthetic treatment may serve as a functional extension of reconstruction rather than a cosmetic adjunct. The central concept is not volumisation, but restoration of tissue quality, dynamic balance and facial function. Prospective studies using validated functional, scar and patient-reported outcome measures are required to define its role in modern oral and maxillofacial surgery.

title: Alus harbor genetic variants that shape the human cortex.
Genome-wide analysis of common structural variants in Alzheimer's disease identifies a risk-associated regulatory CCG repeat in FAM193B.
abstract: Although Alzheimer's disease (AD) has a polygenic architecture, with numerous associated single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) identified, the contribution of structural variants (SVs) is unclear. In this study, using long-read (n = 11) and short-read (n = 3,190) sequencing data from the Chinese population, we show that common SVs contribute to AD heritability beyond common SNPs. We identify an expanded CCG repeat in the FAM193B promoter that shows a genome-wide significant association with increased AD risk (odds ratio = 2.20 per 10-repeat increase, P = 5.5 × 10-13). The expanded FAM193B-CCG repeat increases FAM193B expression and mediates the pleiotropic association between brain FAM193B expression and AD risk. Analyses of postmortem human brains and cultured neuronal cells show that elevated neuronal FAM193B expression is associated with DNA damage and cell death-related pathways. These findings establish the common FAM193B-CCG repeat as an AD risk genetic factor and highlight the contribution of common SVs to AD heritability.

title: Investigating molecular and hemodynamic effects of LSD in the human brain.
abstract: Lysergic acid diethylamide (LSD) is a potent psychedelic with increasing therapeutic interest, yet qualification of target engagement using in vivo neuroimaging has not yet been performed. Using simultaneous positron emission tomography-magnetic resonance imaging technology, we describe multiple brain actions of LSD in seven healthy volunteers blinded to LSD dose received. Here we show that LSD occupies 5-HT2AR with a high affinity and increases both global cerebral blood flow (CBF) and internal carotid artery flow. LSD also decreases global connectivity, which was negatively associated with changes in CBF. We observe an anticlockwise hysteresis loop between plasma drug levels and subjective effects, suggesting atypical pharmacodynamic mechanisms. We contrast our CBF and global connectivity findings and their relation in a separate cohort of 25 participants administered psilocybin, highlighting key consistencies and differences. By establishing the dose-occupancy relation of LSD in humans, our findings provide insights for the clinical development of psychedelic compounds and demonstrate unique neurophysiological effects that distinguish LSD from psilocybin.

title: Autonomic function and signal complexity reflect level and severity of traumatic spinal cord injury.
abstract: Observational single-centre cohort study. To investigate heart rate variability (HRV), baroreflex sensitivity (BRS), and signal complexity (SC) and their relationships with neurological injury level and severity, as well as their prognostic value for six-month mortality and functional recovery in patients with traumatic spinal cord injury (TSCI). Uppsala University Hospital, Sweden. This study included 164 adult patients with TSCI treated in neurointensive care (NIC) (2008-2022). Continuous high-frequency physiological data from the first 7 post-injury days were analysed to derive HRV, BRS, and SC for heart rate (HR), mean arterial pressure, systolic blood pressure, and diastolic blood pressure (DBP). Associations with neurological injury level, injury severity, NIC physiology, neurological improvement, and six-month mortality were assessed. Patients with cervical injuries had higher HRV, BRS (both p < 0.01), and SC for DBP (p < 0.05) than those with thoracic injuries. Complete cervical injuries had higher HRV (p < 0.05), but lower HR SC (p < 0.01) compared with incomplete cervical injuries. Higher HR SC was associated with neurological improvement at discharge (odds ratio 1.08 [95% confidence interval 1.01-1.16]; p < 0.05), whereas higher HRV was associated with increased six-month mortality (odds ratio 1.01 [95% confidence interval 1.00-1.02]; p < 0.05). Other autonomic and complexity measures showed limited prognostic value. Systemic autonomic indices after TSCI vary with injury level and severity and may capture distinct aspects of autonomic dysfunction beyond clinical grading. However, their limited prognostic value for neurological recovery and mortality suggest that outcome prediction after TSCI may depend more on other clinical factors and, possibly, more direct intraspinal physiological markers. title: Testing neurobiological models of reward/incentive sensitization in the continuation of alcohol use disorder (AUD) symptoms in young adults with AUD: A four-year longitudinal study.
journal: Neuropsychopharmacology : official publication of the American College of Neuropsychopharmacology
abstract: Alcohol use disorder (AUD) remains an urgent public health problem. Alcohol response phenotype may be an important factor underlying vulnerability to and progression of AUD. This study examined the prospective association between acute alcohol responses and continued or remitted AUD over time in young adults with AUD. This sample was N = 101 AUD participants (Mage=27.1 ± 4.0 SD yrs) comprising the third cohort of the Chicago Social Drinking Project. They completed two beverage challenge laboratory sessions (0.8 g/kg fixed-dose alcohol vs. placebo) and four years of follow-up to ascertain future AUD symptoms, drinking behaviors, and consequences. Retention was high with an overall 99.2% follow-up rate. Analyses identified three AUD trajectory subgroups over follow-up including a high AUD trajectory subgroup (n = 37), a medium AUD trajectory subgroup (n = 48), and a low AUD trajectory subgroup (n = 16). Generalized estimating equations showed that greater sensitivity to alcohol's pleasurable effects, including stimulation and hedonic and motivational reward (liking and wanting, respectively) predicted more AUD symptoms over follow-up (ps<0.001) and were positively associated with AUD trajectory subgroups. However, sedation, heart rate, and cortisol response to alcohol were not significantly associated with AUD trajectory subgroups. In sum, greater alcohol stimulation, liking, and wanting prospectively predicted the continuation and increasing severity of AUD over a four-year period. The findings challenge theoretical models emphasizing reward deficit and global tolerance in addiction and support the role of positive reinforcement, indexed by sensitivity to alcohol's pleasurable effects, as an important factor in AUD persistence. title: Enhancing cGMP signaling with psilocybin reduces head twitch and restructures the synaptic proteome while maintaining antidepressant response.
journal: Neuropsychopharmacology : official publication of the American College of Neuropsychopharmacology
abstract: Psilocybin produces antidepressant effects, but perceptual effects limit tolerability. We hypothesized that enhancing cGMP signaling with a phosphodiesterase-9 inhibitor (PDE9i) would diminish a rodent behavioral readout of 5-HT₂AR activation, while preserving antidepressant-like effects. PDE9i attenuated psilocybin-induced head-twitch while maintaining the antidepressant-like response. PDE9i-psilocybin reduced 5-HT₂AR-related pathways while enhancing synaptogenesis signaling.

title: Correction: "Increasing dopamine synthesis capacity in the dorsal striatum and tonic acetylcholine: implications for the new muscarinic agents in the treatment of schizophrenia".
Mapping high resolution, multidimensional phase diagrams of near-physiological protein condensates.
abstract: Biomolecular condensates are membraneless compartments, crucial for organising and regulating diverse cellular processes. Current approaches to study condensate biology either use simplified recombinant protein systems with limited physiological relevance, or complex live-cell models with restricted experimental control and scalability. Here, we present ExVivo PhaseScan, a droplet microfluidics platform that couples mammalian lysate-based reconstitution with scalable analysis to generate high-resolution phase diagrams of compositionally complex protein condensates. We apply this approach to study two multicomponent condensate systems, stress granules and nucleoli, and dissect the physicochemical interactions that influence their stability. We further developed a machine learning pipeline to analyse condensate morphology which we use to reveal how mutations in the amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS)-linked protein Fused in Sarcoma (FUS) remodels condensate properties. We identify liquid-to-solid transitions of mutant FUS within stress granules and nucleoli, and show that these transitions can be reversed by RNA aptamer-based interventions. Together, these findings establish ExVivo PhaseScan as a versatile tool for dissecting the physicochemical and pathological regulation of condensates, with potential to inform therapeutic strategies for diseases driven by aberrant phase transitions.

title: Sleep forms flexible context representations in toddlers.
abstract: Sleep consolidates episodic memory through a hippocampus-dependent process in adults. Whether and how sleep supports memory consolidation during early life, when hippocampal function is immature, remains unclear. Here, we examined effects of sleep on the consolidation of spatial context, a core component of episodic memory, in toddlers aged 2-3 years. Toddlers were familiarized with two spatial contexts, followed by a ~ 90-min nap or equivalent wake period. Afterwards, using a hide-and-seek game we tested their ability to relocate toys within these contexts. Only after post-familiarization sleep, toddlers showed significant context memory and formed stronger associations between toys and specific contexts compared to wakefulness. Contextual memory was positively correlated with spindle density and slow oscillation-spindle phase-amplitude coupling during non-rapid eye movement sleep. Here, we show that, despite hippocampal immaturity, memory effects in the sleeping toddler's brain are accompanied by thalamo-cortical oscillatory dynamics that are also implicated in adult memory consolidation.

title: Structural basis of IgLON5 autoantibody recognition in autoimmune encephalitis.
abstract: Anti-IgLON5 disease is a rare neuro-immunological disorder characterized by autoantibodies targeting the neuronal adhesion molecule IgLON5, as well as profound brain dysfunction and tau pathology. Despite its severe clinical manifestations, the molecular basis of antibody recognition and its contribution to disease pathogenesis is poorly understood. Here, we characterize the B cell receptor repertoire of a patient with anti-IgLON5 disease, revealing marked diversity and no evidence of dominant clonal expansion. We isolate a human monoclonal IgG4 antibody that binds IgLON5 with high affinity and determine the structure of its Fab in complex with IgLON5 using cryo-electron microscopy. Biochemical and structural analyses show that antibody binding preserves IgLON5 adhesive interfaces while remaining compatible with clustering of IgLON5 on the cell surface. Analysis of the germline-reverted precursor suggests that IgLON5 recognition is already present before affinity maturation and is strengthened by somatic mutations that stabilize antigen binding. These findings provide mechanistic insight into autoantibody recognition of neuronal surface proteins and establish a framework for understanding antibody-mediated neurodegeneration in anti-IgLON5 disease.

title: Progress in pain mechanisms and management.
abstract: Pain is a multifaceted sensory and emotional experience that profoundly affects human health and quality of life. It functions as a double-edged sword: while acute pain serves as a protective warning signal, chronic pain compromises physiological and psychological well-being. Pain is now widely regarded as the "fifth vital sign," and given its rising prevalence and substantial global burden, chronic pain may also be considered a major chronic disease entity. Accordingly, elucidating the neural and molecular underpinnings of pain and developing effective analgesic strategies remain urgent priorities. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the molecular and neural circuit mechanisms that govern pain. At the molecular level, ion channels, diverse receptor systems, and intricate signaling pathways play central roles in the transduction and modulation of nociceptive signals. At the circuit level, pain processing involves ascending pathways, descending modulatory systems, and distributed brain regions that collectively encode the sensory and affective dimensions of pain. Building on these mechanistic insights, we discuss current therapeutic strategies, including pharmacological and nonpharmacological interventions, as well as emerging approaches such as gene therapy, stem cell-based therapies and neuromodulation. Despite notable progress, several challenges remain, including the adverse effects associated with existing analgesics and an incomplete understanding of visceral pain mechanisms. Future research should prioritize the integration of multiomics approaches, advanced neural circuit mapping technologies, and artificial intelligence to refine mechanistic insights and enable the development of more precise and effective pain management strategies.

title: Endothelial cell-microglia crosstalk mediates heart failure-associated synaptic loss and cognitive impairment in male mice.
abstract: Cognitive impairment affects 30%-80% of patients with heart failure, yet the mechanisms beyond reduced brain blood flow remain poorly defined. Here we show that circulating factors released during heart failure trigger senescence of brain blood-vessel endothelial cells, which in turn drives synaptic loss and cognitive decline through crosstalk between endothelial cells and microglia, the brain's immune cells. Using a pressure-overload model (transverse aortic constriction) combined with plasma transfer in 8-month-old male mice, we found that elevated circulating TGFβ2 acts on endothelial TGFBR2 and induces the secreted protein SPARC via a non-canonical MEK/ERK-MYC pathway. Endothelial SPARC then activates microglial TLR4, promoting neuroinflammation and abnormal engulfment of synapses. Endothelial deletion of Tgfbr2 or Sparc, and microglial deletion of Tlr4, each preserved synapses and improved cognition, and pharmacological Tlr4 inhibition was protective. These findings define an endothelial-microglia signaling axis and a potential therapeutic target in heart failure-associated cognitive impairment.

title: Assessing the effect of subthalamic stimulation on metaperception in obsessive-compulsive disorder.
abstract: Most human studies on perceptual decision-making are correlational, and few addressed the causal role of the neural markers they identify. Here, we took the opportunity offered by deep brain stimulation to study the causal role of subthalamo-cortical networks on perceptual decision-making and perceptual monitoring. We asked participants with obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) treated with subthalamic stimulation to detect visual stimuli and provide confidence reports while we recorded scalp electroencephalography. Following a preregistered plan, we compared behavioural and neural results between patients off-stimulation and matched healthy controls and among patients on and off-stimulation to identify the effect of subthalamic stimulation on perceptual choices and metacognitive judgments. Our results indicate that patients off-stimulation detected visual stimuli similarly to matched healthy controls but provided poorer confidence judgments, indicative of a potential metacognitive alteration. Moreover, chronic subthalamic stimulation significantly reduced clinical symptoms, but acute stimulation changes did not impact visual detection, confidence, nor corresponding event-related potentials at the scalp level. We conclude that acute changes in subthalamic stimulation are insufficient to modify the potential metacognitive alterations observed in OCD.

title: Surviving the Storm: A Qualitative Study of Caregivers' Challenges in Family-Based Treatment for Adolescent Anorexia Nervosa.
journal: The International journal of eating disorders
abstract: Family-based treatment (FBT) is the recommended first-line outpatient treatment for adolescent anorexia nervosa (AN) in Aotearoa New Zealand (NZ), but places substantial responsibility on parents/caregivers. Although caregiver burden in FBT is increasingly recognized internationally, in-depth qualitative work situated in the NZ service context is lacking. This study explored how caregivers experienced participating in FBT for adolescent AN in NZ. Twelve caregivers participated in semi-structured interviews between May and July 2025. Interviews were analyzed within an interpretive description framework using reflexive thematic analysis. Three themes were developed: confronting a life-threatening illness within an under-resourced and often unresponsive healthcare system; implementing an overwhelming, isolating treatment with limited guidance; and living with the lingering psychological toll long after FBT concluded. Caregivers described experiences relating to caring for someone with AN and supporting them through treatment as consistent with trauma-implicated stressors, although traumatic stress was not formally assessed. These findings show how systemic, structural, and relational factors intersect to shape caregivers' experiences and highlight the need for better-resourced, trauma-informed adaptations of FBT that position caregivers and young people as co-central partners in care.

title: Electrophysiologic Demyelinating Features Are Common in Vasculitic Neuropathy: A Cohort of Biopsy-Confirmed Cases.
abstract: Electrophysiologic features suggestive of demyelination have been reported in vasculitic neuropathy, complicating the diagnostic process, but their frequency is unknown. We aimed to determine the prevalence of demyelinating features, including fulfillment of European Academy of Neurology/Peripheral Nerve Society (EAN/PNS) electrophysiological criteria for demyelination in suspected CIDP, in a cohort of patients with biopsy-confirmed vasculitic neuropathy. Clinical data and nerve conduction studies from patients with biopsy-confirmed vasculitic neuropathy (definite or probable) were retrospectively analyzed in two centers in France between 2014 and 2020. Sixty-three patients were included (mean age 58 ± 16 years; 30% were male), including 28 with non-systemic vasculitic neuropathy (NSVN) and 35 with systemic vasculitic neuropathy (SVN). Pain and sensory disturbances were present in all patients, whereas motor deficits occurred in 73% of patients. The predominant electrophysiological pattern was a symmetrical distal polyneuropathy (n = 26). Twenty-seven (42.9%) patients showed demyelinating NCS abnormalities, and 11 (17.5%) patients fulfilled the EAN/PNS criteria for demyelination. Motor conduction block was the most frequent demyelinating abnormality, followed by prolonged F-wave latency. Demyelinating abnormalities were present in 7.1% of NSVN patients and 25.7% of SVN patients, with no statistically significant difference between groups. Electrophysiological patterns suggestive of demyelination are common in vasculitic neuropathy. Nevertheless, most patients presented with pain and a symmetrical distal polyneuropathy, a phenotype not typically associated with demyelinating neuropathy. Future studies integrating detailed clinical data may help identify key diagnostic features and improve recognition despite potentially misleading electrodiagnostic findings.

Enhanced pitch perception in early blind individuals and musicians is due to reduced internal noise.
journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
abstract: Although it is commonly assumed that early blind individuals have enhanced pitch perception, the literature to date has been contradictory. We measured performance on two tasks known to recruit early versus late stages of auditory frequency tuning in early blind and sighted human adults of both sexes with matched years of musical training. The two groups showed equivalent performance on a tone detection in notched-noise task that assesses cochlear frequency selectivity. In contrast, early blind individuals showed enhanced performance in a pitch discrimination task thought to be mediated by cortical mechanisms. Computational modeling revealed that this enhancement was best explained by reduced internal noise rather than narrower frequency tuning, with both blindness and years of musical training predicting a reduction in internal noise. These findings identify internal noise as a key factor in experience-driven auditory plasticity as a result of both musical experience and early blindness.Significance Statement For centuries, early blindness has been associated with superior auditory abilities. Here we find that the enhanced pitch perception in early blind individuals is best explained by reduced internal noise at higher levels of auditory processing, rather than sharper frequency tuning. Years of musical training similarly resulted in lower internal noise, suggesting a shared mechanism through which experience improves auditory perception. These findings identify internal noise reduction as a key component of experience-dependent auditory plasticity.

Aspects of hand use development in infants aged 4 to 18 months with or at risk of cerebral palsy: a longitudinal study.
abstract: Promoting hand use is a key goal in the rehabilitation of infants with or at risk of cerebral palsy (CP). To inform treatment planning, this study aimed to describe aspects of hand use development in these infants aged four to 18 months. Longitudinal design with repeated measurements using the Hand Assessment for Infants (HAI) from four to 12 months of age. At 18 months of age, the Assisting Hand Assessment (AHA), Both Hand Assessment (BoHA), Peabody Developmental Motor Scale (PDMS-2), and mini-MACS (Manual Ability Classification System) were applied. Descriptive statistics identified developmental trajectories for hand use. Linear mixed models estimated growth curves among infants diagnosed with CP. Associations between HAI scores at six and 8 months and outcomes at 18 months were examined using Spearman rank correlation and regression analyses. In total, 41 infants with or at risk of CP participated. Developmental hand use trajectories for each infant showed a clear pattern, with trajectories clustering according to manual ability at 18 months, classified by mini-MACS level for infants with CP (bilateral [n = 17], unilateral [n = 12]) and as "typical manual ability" for infants without CP (n = 12). Growth curve, defined by CP subtype and mini-MACS level at 18 months, showed modest differences between groups in the early months, relatively weak linear improvement in HAI scores over time in infants with higher mini-MACS, steeper gains over time in infants with lower mini-MACS, and a similar pattern with overlapping confidence intervals for the two CP subtype within the same mini-MACS level. A strong negative correlation was found between HAI scores and mini-MACS level. Regression analyses demonstrated a statistically significant and positive association between HAI scores and BoHA, AHA, or PDMS-2 subtest (Visual-Motor Integration) scores. HAI scores at 6 months of age may indicate the subsequent development of hand use up to 18 months of age. This contributes important knowledge to early treatment planning. The results must be interpreted with caution due to the small sample size. Larger studies are needed before firm conclusions are made.

title: Impact of Host α2-Antiplasmin Deficiency on Engraftment and the Morphological Maturation of Transplanted Neural Precursor Cells in the Mouse Brain.
abstract: Neural precursor cell (NPC) transplantation is a promising therapeutic strategy for reconstructing damaged neuronal circuits and achieving functional recovery in neurological diseases. However, the impact of the host microenvironment on the survival and maturation of transplanted cells is not fully understood. The fibrinolytic system regulates clot lysis and extracellular matrix remodeling through proteolytic activity, but its role in neuronal maturation following NPC transplantation remains to be elucidated. This study investigated whether host deficiency of α2-antiplasmin (α2AP), the primary inhibitor of plasmin, affects the engraftment and maturation of transplanted NPCs in the mouse brain. Green fluorescent protein-expressing mouse embryonic stem cell-derived NPCs were transplanted into the brains of wild-type (WT) and α2AP-knockout (KO) mice. Graft size and cell survival were comparable between WT and α2AP-KO mice, suggesting that host α2AP deficiency does not affect engraftment efficiency. In contrast, the number of neurites in transplanted neurons tended to be lower in α2AP-KO mice, particularly in DCX-positive immature neurons. These findings suggest that α2AP in the host environment may contribute to the morphological maturation of transplanted neurons rather than to their survival and differentiation.

title: [ACCEPTANCE OF EPINEPHRINE NASAL SPRAY (NEFFY®) AMONG PEDIATRIC EPIPEN® CARRIERS AND THEIR PARENTS PRIOR TO ITS LAUNCH IN JAPAN].
abstract: Epinephrine nasal spray (Neffy®) demonstrates pharmacodynamic effects comparable to epinephrine auto-injector (EpiPen®) and is considered safe. Neffy was approved in Japan on September 19, 2025, as an "Adjunctive treatment for anaphylactic reactions" and launched on February 12, 2026. It is expected to become a new option for initial anaphylaxis treatment. To investigate the acceptance of the new formulation and the background factors influencing that acceptance among pediatric patients and their parents who carry EpiPen before Neffy's distribution. A questionnaire was delivered online or on paper to pediatric patients carrying EpiPen and their parents/guardians who visited our hospital between November 18 and December 26, 2025. Although awareness was still low before Neffy's distribution, the majority of patients and parents were interested in Neffy. Parents who were more accepting of Neffy reported higher anxiety about carrying EpiPens and had lower confidence in their use. In several cases, a discrepancy existed between the patient's and their parent's acceptance. Moving forward, treatment selection should be based on accurate information and in consultation with both patients and their parents.

title: Ellipsoid zone defects in age-related macular degeneration: the Beijing Eye Study.
Moyamoya-Type Collaterals in ACTA2 p. Arg179 Related Arteriopathy: Challenging the Paradigm of Absent Neovascularization-A Longitudinal DSA Study.
abstract: ACTA2 p. Arg179 variants can cause a distinctive cerebrovascular arteriopathy historically described lacking classic moyamoya basal collaterals. Limited data on collateral architecture and surgical outcomes have led to uncertainty regarding revascularization strategies. The purpose of this study is to provide a systematic longitudinal DSA assessment of collateral patterns and postoperative findings in pediatric ACTA2-associated cerebrovascular disease. Ten pediatric patients with genetically confirmed ACTA2 mutations underwent DSA imaging. Eight consecutive patients with neurological instability and confirmed hemodynamic compromise underwent surgical revascularization (indirect or combined direct-indirect). Two patients with stable neurological status were managed conservatively. Paired DSA (7 patients) and magnetic resonance angiography (5 patients) were performed at baseline and follow-up of the operated cohort. Collaterals were classified as classic moyamoya-type, distal moyamoya-type, leptomeningeal, or duropial. Postoperative revascularization was graded using Matsushima classification. Mean baseline vessel calibers demonstrated marked proximal ectasia (petrous ICA 8.4 ± 2.8 mm vs. normative 3.8 ± 0.4) transitioning to distal stenosis (supraclinoid ICA 2.6 ± 0.7 mm vs. normative 3.3 ± 0.3). Classic moyamoya-type collaterals were present in 2 patients at baseline and in 5 patients at follow-up. Postoperative Matsushima grading demonstrated Grade A/B in 6 patients, with surgical collateralization remaining patent and sufficient up to 14 years. ACTA2 p. Arg179 related cerebral arteriopathy demonstrates moyamoya-type collaterals challenging the historical paradigm of absent collateralization. Robust surgical neovascularization comparable to idiopathic moyamoya may support revascularization in symptomatic pediatric patients with confirmed hemodynamic compromise.

title: Imaging of Neurodegenerative Disorders of the Spinal Cord.
abstract: This article aims to provide a comprehensive review of imaging features of non-compressive spinal cord degeneration. It covers a range of disorders including multiple sclerosis, motor neuron disease, hereditary ataxias, metabolic myelopathies, and acquired conditions. The article highlights the diagnostic limitations of conventional MRI and points out the role of advanced quantitative techniques such as diffusion tensor imaging and magnetization transfer imaging in detecting structural changes that underpin early disease. It concludes by outlining the pathway for integrating conventional and advanced imaging techniques with the clinical picture to reach an accurate diagnosis.

title: Imaging of Spinal Cord Inflammatory Disorders.
abstract: Inflammatory myelopathies comprise a group of spinal cord disorders with overlapping clinical manifestations but distinct etiologies, prognoses, and treatment implications. This article highlights the role of magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) in differentiating immune-mediated causes of myelitis, including multiple sclerosis, aquaporin-4-positive neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder, myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody-associated disease, glial fibrillary acidic protein astrocytopathy, immune checkpoint inhibitor-related neuroinflammatory conditions, paraneoplastic syndromes, and systemic autoimmune diseases. MRI patterns, including longitudinal lesion length, axial distribution, enhancement characteristics, and temporal evolution, are discussed alongside clinical/paraclinical correlates. Disease-specific imaging features, common mimics, and emerging imaging techniques are examined.

title: Imaging of Spinal Cord Trauma.
abstract: This article outlines the evolving role of MRI in traumatic spinal cord injury (SCI) across acute to chronic stages. Conventional MRI remains indispensable for diagnosis and early prognosis, while quantitative morphometrics such as tissue bridges and spinal cord cross-sectional area provide robust and clinically applicable predictors of post-SCI recovery. Advanced techniques, including diffusion, myelin-sensitive, and functional MRI, enable the detection of microstructural damage, remote neurodegeneration, and functional reorganization. Ongoing advances in scan protocol standardization, automated image analysis, and AI-driven lesion segmentation are expected to improve reproducibility and facilitate the integration of imaging biomarkers into clinical practice and interventional trials.

title: Imaging of Degenerative Cervical and Thoracic Myelopathy.
abstract: In this article, we focus on imaging of degenerative cervical myelopathy, the most common form of spinal cord dysfunction in adults arising from its progressive compression by age-related degenerative changes in the spine. Imaging plays a key role in confirming the underlying cause of symptoms and guiding neurosurgical intervention. Emerging imaging methods promise earlier diagnosis, better prognostication, and more accurate identification of candidates for surgical intervention. Differences in imaging findings for the less prevalent degenerative thoracic myelopathy are also discussed.

title: "It takes us out of our daily lives": Lived experience and healthcare provider perspectives on virtual nature travel during psychiatric hospitalization.
abstract: Psychiatric hospitalizations can be highly stressful and may offer limited opportunities for meaningful, recovery-oriented interventions. Immersive virtual reality (VR) may provide accessible leisure and social experiences, but little is known about how hospitalized individuals and healthcare providers perceive its use in inpatient psychiatric care. Semi-structured qualitative interviews were conducted with hospitalized individuals (n = 29) and online surveys were collected from healthcare providers (n = 7), following the implementation of Toujours Dimanche, an immersive virtual-nature travel application with a social component, on an inpatient unit for complex mood disorders. Thematic analyses were conducted. Participants described the application as a temporary break from the experience of psychiatric hospitalization that provided stimulation, emotional respite, social connection, and opportunities to reconnect with life beyond the unit. Although hospitalized individuals and healthcare providers generally viewed the service positively, they identified several conditions affecting its sustained implementation, including perceptions of patient suitability, limited staffing and space, and uncertainty regarding the value of recovery-oriented benefits in the absence of demonstrated symptom improvement. Virtual nature travel was perceived as a meaningful adjunct to inpatient psychiatric care. Its sustainable integration may depend on adequate institutional resources and greater recognition of well-being and recovery-oriented outcomes as legitimate aims of hospitalization.

title: Long-Term Treatment Patterns in Norwegian ADHD-Medicine Users: A Cohort Register-Based Study With 5 Years of Follow-Up, 2012-2021.
abstract: To improve interpretation of long-term ADHD medication treatment trajectories in Norway by examining sex- and age-specific persistence, distinguishing within-substance product switching from active-ingredient (ATC substance) switching, and describing the medication and prescriber context of the last observed dispensation before non-persistence. This study used population-based data from the Norwegian Prescription Database (NorPD) to identify 33 706 incident users initiating ADHD medication in 2012-2016, defined using an individual-specific 5-year look-back. Participants were followed for up to 5 years until 2021. We estimated dispensing-based persistence, defined non-persistence as the first dispensing gap of ≥ 396 days/13 months, characterised switching as either within-substance product switching or active-ingredient (ATC substance) switching, and described the last dispensed medication and prescriber specialty recorded before non-persistence. The cohort included 19 898 men (59%) and 13 808 women (41%); 97%-98% initiated methylphenidate. Five-year persistence was 39% in men and 35% in women. During follow-up, 41% had no switch and 26% had ≥ 4 switches. Among first switches, within-substance product switching predominated (80.9% in men; 77.5% in women), while active-ingredient switching was less common (19.1% and 22.5%, respectively). Among those who met the non-persistence definition during follow-up (62.4%), the last dispensed medication was methylphenidate (76%), atomoxetine/guanfacine (12%), lisdexamfetamine (7%), and dexamphetamine (3%), respectively; the last prescriber specialty recorded on the last dispensation was a general practitioner for 51.9% and a specialist for 48.1%. In Norway, most incident ADHD medication users met a dispensing-based definition of non-persistence within 5 years. Switching was frequent, but most first switches occurred within the same active substance rather than between substances, suggesting that many observed changes in dispensing data may reflect product substitution or formulation change rather than a true change in pharmacological strategy. These findings may improve interpretation of long-term treatment trajectories.

title: PTGS2/COX-2 is associated with neurovascular and blood-brain barrier changes in behaviourally classified MRL/lpr mice.

Augmentation strategies for intravenous ketamine in treatment-resistant depression: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: Treatment-resistant depression (TRD) affects 30-60% of individuals with major depressive disorder and carries substantial morbidity and healthcare costs. Intravenous (IV) ketamine (KET) is a rapid-acting antidepressant, but benefits are often transient, prompting augmentation to sustain efficacy or improve tolerability. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) of IV KET augmentation in adults with TRD. MEDLINE, Embase, and PsycINFO were searched through October 29, 2025. Eligible studies compared KET plus augmentation with KET plus placebo/sham or active control. Seven RCTs (N = 346) met inclusion criteria. Strategies included glutathione, riluzole, lamotrigine, lithium, D-cycloserine, cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT), and automated self-association training (ASAT). Across the included trials, IV KET was associated with antidepressant improvement, although augmentation strategies generally did not demonstrate additional benefit over their respective control conditions. Pharmacological augmentation strategies did not demonstrate additional benefit at primary endpoints. KCP approaches using CBT and ASAT yielded preliminary signals of improved maintenance of antidepressant effects, although each was evaluated in a single study. An exploratory random-effects meta-analysis of seven heterogeneous comparisons found no statistically significant overall difference in depressive symptoms between augmentation and control conditions (SMD = -0.12; 95% CI, -0.37 to 0.12; p = 0.323; I2 = 0.0%). No new safety signal emerged in the trials, although adverse-event reporting was heterogeneous across studies. Overall, low-certainty randomized evidence is insufficient to support routine augmentation of IV ketamine for TRD, highlighting the need for larger, rigorously designed trials to determine whether specific strategies can meaningfully extend ketamine's antidepressant effects.

title: Post-stroke depression, but not anxiety, is independently associated with executive and visuospatial function: A five-year longitudinal cohort study.
abstract: Post-stroke anxiety and depression frequently co-occur, and whether each is independently associated with cognitive impairment remains unclear because most studies model one without adjusting for the other. In a five-year cohort, we tested whether anxiety and depression have distinct cognitive correlates and whether 6-month affective status predicted subsequent cognitive recovery. Patients from the STROKDEM cohort (n = 191) were assessed at 6, 12, 36, and 60 months post-stroke for anxiety, depression, and five cognitive domains (memory, executive functioning, attention, visuospatial functioning, and language). Two symmetric random-intercept linear mixed models regressed each affective score on the cognitive domains while adjusting for the other. Repeated-measures correlations, multiple imputation for attrition, and exploratory trajectory and prognostic models were also used. After mutual adjustment and correction, depression was independently associated with executive and visuospatial function, whereas anxiety showed no independent cognitive correlate. Repeated-measures correlations confirmed this dissociation. The executive association and the absence of an anxiety correlate were robust to all sensitivity analyses, including multiple imputation for attrition, whereas the visuospatial association was attrition-sensitive. Exploratory associations between 6-month affect and cognitive recovery did not survive multiple imputation and were inconclusive. Attrition was substantial and selective on baseline cognition; the persistent-anxiety subgroup was small; and psychiatric history, psychotropic medication, and cognitive reserve beyond education were unavailable. The cognitive burden of post-stroke affective disorders is carried by depression rather than anxiety. Screening for depression, rather than anxiety alone, may better identify stroke survivors at cognitive risk.

title: Differential changes in frontolimbic functional connectivity following 12-week psychostimulant monotherapy in ADHD youth with and without familial risk for bipolar I disorder.
abstract: Although attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), psychostimulant medications, and BD family history are risk factors for developing bipolar I disorder (BD), their contribution to the aberrant ventrolateral prefrontal cortex (VLPFC) and amygdala (AMY) functional connectivity (FC) implicated in the pathophysiology of BD remain unclear. We investigated the effects of 12-week daily oral psychostimulant monotherapy on AMY-VLPFC FC during emotional and task-related attentional processing in ADHD youth with ('high-risk', HR) and without ('low-risk', LR) a first-degree relative with BD. LR received mixed amphetamine salts-extended release (MAS) and HR were randomized to MAS or placebo (PLA). Functional magnetic resonance scans were acquired at baseline and week 12 during a continuous performance task with emotional distracters. Generalized psychophysiological interaction analysis assessed AMY-VLPFC FC during emotional and task-related attentional processing. The study included 116 youth [healthy controls n = 38, LR-MAS n = 42, HR-MAS n = 24, HR-PLA n = 12]. Following treatment, neither LR-MAS nor HR-MAS exhibited changes in bilateral AMY-VLPFC FC during emotional processing. During task-related attentional processing, HR-MAS youth showed greater longitudinal increase in right AMY-VLPFC negative FC compared with LR-MAS (P = 0.034) and HR-PLA groups (P = 0.007). Compared with HR-MAS, LR-MAS exhibited greater reductions in ADHD total and inattention symptoms. These findings suggest that familial BD risk may be associated with a differential longitudinal neurofunctional response to a regimen of psychostimulant monotherapy during attentional, but not emotional, processing.

title: Machine learning in the prediction of binge drinking: A systematic review.
abstract: Binge drinking (BD) refers to episodes of excessive alcohol consumption, which are associated with various acute and long-term consequences. Despite its high prevalence and negative impacts, predictive features for BD remain lacking. This study aims to review machine learning (ML) research on BD, comparing different algorithms and types of data, trying to identify promising models and variables that may help identify individuals at risk. A systematic search was performed in PubMed, Embase, and Scopus to identify relevant studies published before July 2, 2026. 21 studies were included in data extraction process. The results suggest that impulsive factors, substance-use variables, emotional distress, as well as demographic features, particularly gender and age, play a significant role in predicting BD. Moreover, emerging methods that use real-time data recorded via mobile apps showed promise. Conversely, findings from neural data yielded mixed results, with no single brain area consistently associated with BD. The qualitative comparison did not show any specific ML algorithm consistently outperforming the others across studies; however, the predictive performance of ML approaches tended to improve when different data types were combined. The analysis of the available literature was restricted due to the non-homogeneous characteristics of studies, mainly in terms of methodology, which did not allow us to draw comprehensive conclusions. The comparison of available ML studies showed how promising risk factors can be combined within multivariate models to increase their predictive value. Future large-scale studies using multisource data may better define risk profiles to foster prevention strategies.

title: Adverse drug reactions associated with psychotropic medications combined with versus without lithium: A case/control pharmacovigilance analysis.
abstract: We assessed the association between different adverse drug reactions (ADRs) and patients with versus without lithium co-medication using data from the European drug surveillance program AMSP (German: "Arzneimittelsicherheit in der Psychiatrie," i.e. Drug Safety in Psychiatry)Methods:We conducted a case/non-case pharmacovigilance study using AMSP data on ADRs from patients treated in psychiatric hospitals in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland. We performed a disproportionality analysis of reports of severe ADRs from patients with versus without lithium co-medication calculating reporting odds ratios (RORs). Additional analyses included comparisons with distinct pharmacological classes, reports where the imputation grade for ADRs was probable or certain, and where ADR rates were related to exposed patients. In 8609 patients, lithium-treated patients (n = 720) were less often associated with weight gain, dyskinesia, suicidality (as an ADR), hyponatremia, and mortality, but more often associated with various types of neurotoxicity (p < 0.05 in all cases). Parkinson's symptoms (ROR 1.8), tremor (ROR 4.6), serotonergic ADRs (ROR 3.0), ataxia or myoclonus (each, ROR 2.7), as well as drug-drug interactions leading to intoxication (ROR 26.3, p < 0.05 in all cases). When stratifying by pharmacological class, hyponatremia was more frequent in patients receiving different pharmacological classes (p < 0.05 in all cases), whereas neurotoxicity and lithium intoxications were more frequently reported in lithium comedication groups (p < 0.05 in all cases). Patients treated with lithium are associated with a reduced reporting of hyponatremia, but to an increased reporting of neurotoxicity, although findings represent reporting associations, rather than incidence estimates or causal effects.

title: Clinical Markers of Vulnerability for Bleeding in Men With Prostate Cancer and Antithrombotic Treatment.
abstract: Men with prostate cancer have a high risk for bleeding when treated with antithrombotics. The aim of this study was to investigate clinical markers for vulnerability for bleeding in these men the last year of life. This is a retrospective study on deceased patients with advanced prostate cancer admitted to specialized palliative care and treated with antithrombotics the last year of life. Relative risk (RR) was calculated with log-binomial models. Of 100 men with end-stage prostate cancer, 64 men were treated with antithrombotics. Twenty-four of these (37.5%) suffered from bleeding during the last year of life. Clinical markers associated with an increased vulnerability for bleeding were need of blood transfusion, RR 3.15 (95% CI: 1.34-7.39); low thrombocyte count, RR 2.41 (95% CI: 1.39-4.16); and deep venous thrombosis treatment, RR 2.44 (95% CI: 1.21-4.94). Age, type of antithrombotic, use of steroids, or NSAID were not risk factors. In 50%, antithrombotic treatment continued during the last week in life. Antithrombotic treatment the last year of life is associated with a high risk of bleeding in men with prostate cancer. Clinical markers associated with increased vulnerability for bleeding are low thrombocyte count and need of transfusions.

title: Soluble Indicators of Endothelial Injury and Activation Emerge During Acute HIV Infection and Persist Despite Rapid Antiretroviral Therapy Initiation.
abstract: Vascular activation occurs during human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection and is a risk factor for cardiovascular disease (CVD). This study investigates whether vascular endothelial and hemostatic perturbations emerge during acute HIV infection (AHI) and persist despite immediate antiretroviral therapy (ART) initiation. Thirteen plasma biomarkers indicative of endothelial and hemostatic perturbations were measured in 83 RV254 AHI cohort participants during pre-ART AHI and at week 288 post-ART, compared with cross-sectional measures from 32 people without HIV (PWoH). Hierarchical clustering was applied to week 288 biomarker profiles of RV254 participants and PWoH to identify distinct biomarker phenotypes. During pre-ART AHI, RV254 participants exhibited higher intercellular adhesion molecule-1 (ICAM-1), vascular cell adhesion molecule-1 (VCAM-1), tissue factor, neopterin, and myeloperoxidase than PWoH (P < .05), independent of age, sex, and body mass index (BMI). These markers correlated with plasma HIV RNA or the CD4/CD8 ratio (P < .05). At week 288, significant reductions in ICAM-1, VCAM-1, vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF)-C, VEGF-D, neopterin, and myeloperoxidase and a significant increase in tissue plasminogen activator were observed in RV254 (P < .05). However, VCAM-1 and thrombomodulin remained higher, and VEGF-A remained lower in RV254 participants compared to PWoH (P < .05). Hierarchical clustering identified 2 distinct clusters. Despite comparable 10-year CVD risk, 1 cluster exhibited concomitant elevation of ICAM-1, ICAM-2, VCAM-1, and E-selectin. Notably, 45% of RV254 participants vs 13% of PWoH were classified into this phenotype. Endothelial and hemostatic perturbations emerge during AHI and correlate with HIV-related parameters. Despite suppressive ART, RV254 participants remained approximately 3.5 times more likely than PWoH to exhibit an endothelial activation biomarker phenotype.

title: Drug Use Patterns and Characteristics by Drug Type Among Drug Abusers: Findings From the Survey of Drug Abusers in Korea 2021.
abstract: Although substance use disorders are increasingly recognized in the Republic of Korea (South Korea), empirical data on the prevalence and characteristics of drug use among treatment-seeking populations remain limited. This study examined the rate and temporal patterns of major psychoactive substance use-specifically sedatives/hypnotics/tranquilizers (sedatives), amphetamines, and marijuana/cannabis (cannabis)-across three timeframes and explored the associated sociodemographic and clinical factors. Data were obtained from 540 adults with a history of substance use, recruited from medical and rehabilitation institutions as part of the 2021 Survey of Drug Abusers in Korea. Sociodemographic and clinical factors-including Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, 5th edition (DSM-5)-based substance use disorder (SUD) diagnosis, self-recognition of addiction, depression, anxiety, and Addiction Severity Index (ASI) scores-were assessed. Group comparisons were conducted using χ² and t-tests. Multivariable logistic regression identified factors associated with sedative, amphetamine, and cannabis use across past 30-day, past-year, and lifetime periods. Multiple linear regression examined associations between each substance and ASI composite domains. Statistical significance was set at P < 0.05. Among the 540 individuals with a history of substance use, the lifetime rate of use was highest for amphetamines (71.9%), followed by cannabis (52.8%) and sedatives (38.1%). Sedative use remained relatively consistent across timeframes (30-day: 21.9%; 1-year: 28.9%; lifetime: 38.1%), suggesting patterns of chronic or concurrent use. Across all three substance groups, participants exhibited poorer mental health, including elevated levels of depression, anxiety, or psychiatric severity. Amphetamine and sedative users were more likely to be female, older, and of lower socioeconomic and educational status, with greater impairment in psychiatric, family, and social functioning, as well as higher self-recognition of addiction. In contrast, cannabis users were predominantly younger males with higher socioeconomic status but elevated anxiety levels. Institutional affiliation also differed by substance type: cannabis users were more frequently associated with rehabilitation centers, whereas amphetamine users were more often treated in medical institutions. Findings highlight the coexistence of shared psychosocial vulnerabilities and substance-specific risk profiles in Korea. Integrated, multidimensional interventions-linking psychiatric care, social support, and economic protection-are needed for amphetamine and sedative users. For younger cannabis users, early intervention and relapse prevention are essential. Strengthening coordination between medical and rehabilitation systems under Korea's Judicial-Treatment-Rehabilitation Linkage Model may reduce stigma and enhance recovery-oriented care for individuals with SUD.

title: Preterm Birth Causes Decreased Postnatal Neurogenesis: A Novel Mechanism Underlying Adverse Neurodevelopmental Outcomes.
journal: Pediatrics international : official journal of the Japan Pediatric Society
abstract: Although the survival rates of preterm infants have markedly improved, their neurodevelopmental outcomes remain poor. Historically, brain injury in preterm infants has been recognized as intraventricular hemorrhage or white matter injury, often resulting in cerebral palsy. More recently, increasing attention has focused on the elevated risk of neurodevelopmental disorders among preterm infants across a wide range of gestational ages. Furthermore, preterm birth is also associated with an increased risk of psychiatric disorders in adulthood, including depression and schizophrenia. However, the underlying pathophysiology of these conditions remains poorly understood, and therapeutic strategies and their efficacy are limited. Preterm birth occurs during a critical period of brain development, when processes including neurogenesis, gliogenesis, and oligodendrocyte maturation are actively progressing. In addition, recent studies have demonstrated that in humans, neural stem cells (NSCs) persist in the ventricular-subventricular zone (V-SVZ) during the early postnatal period and continue to generate new neurons. Early postnatal neurogenesis may therefore contribute to brain development during infancy. Although preterm birth may disrupt these developmental processes, its impact on brain development during this critical period remains incompletely understood. We recently discovered that preterm birth causes decreased early postnatal neurogenesis in the V-SVZ in both mice and humans, and proposed this as a novel mechanism underlying adverse neurodevelopmental outcomes in preterm infants. These findings indicate that targeting postnatal NSC function may provide a new therapeutic approach for neurodevelopmental disorders in preterm infants. Our findings also provide new insights into the mechanisms underlying various long-term complications of preterm birth.

title: MAFG as a Redox-Sensitive Node Linking Peripheral Immune Reprogramming to Cognitive Risk in the Sepsis-to-Alzheimer's Disease Continuum: Single-Cell Dissection and Adoptive-Transfer Validation.
abstract: Sepsis survivors face an elevated long-term risk of Alzheimer's disease (AD), yet the peripheral pathways linking systemic immune activation to chronic neurodegeneration remain undefined. We mapped peripheral immune reprogramming across sepsis and AD and tested a candidate regulatory node. A single-cell atlas of peripheral immunity was built by integrating scRNA-seq from human sepsis and AD cohorts, using clustering, SCENIC regulatory-network inference and an exploratory pseudotime ordering. The resulting signature was validated in two clinical cohorts (ROC and survival analysis). MAFG-associated subpopulations and redox status were profiled in APP/PS1, cecal ligation and puncture (CLP) and composite models, and causality was tested by lentiviral MAFG knockdown and adoptive transfer into APP/PS1 recipients. Peripheral immunity was myeloid-skewed in sepsis and lymphoid-dominated in AD, with APP-expressing common myeloid progenitors (CMPs), dendritic cells (DCs), and platelets forming an APP-enriched compartment. A core transcription-factor network differed between disease states, yielding a four-gene signature (MAFG, NFIL3, RGS10, FOXO3) with cross-cohort diagnostic and prognostic value. MAFG was upregulated in septic patients and associated with poorer survival, subpopulation expansion, and systemic oxidative stress. Superimposed CLP aggravated amyloid deposition, microglial activation, and memory deficits in APP/PS1 mice, whereas MAFG silencing restored Aβ uptake and, on adoptive transfer, reduced amyloid burden, attenuated microgliosis, and preserved cognition. Peripheral immune states differ across the sepsis-to-AD spectrum and are captured by a MAFG-centered signature. Independent of any trajectory assumption, loss-of-function and adoptive-transfer experiments identify MAFG as a causal, redox-sensitive node constraining peripheral Aβ clearance and a candidate biomarker and therapeutic target in sepsis survivors.

title: Highly potent, brain-penetrant EP2 receptor antagonists for the treatment of permanent focal cerebral ischaemia in male and female mice.
abstract: Cerebral ischaemia is a leading cause of death in older adults and imposes a substantial global economic burden. Recent studies indicate that inhibiting the Gαs-coupled EP2 receptor reduces ischaemic brain injury by modulating neuroinflammation. However, these findings derive from the transient middle cerebral artery occlusion (tMCAO) model, which represents only a small subset of large-vessel occlusion (LVO) cases with successful recanalisation. We characterised the pharmacokinetic parameters of selective EP2 antagonists CJ-18, CJ-19 and CJ-21 that we recently developed. We evaluated their therapeutic efficacy in mice subjected to permanent MCAO (pMCAO), a model that more accurately reflects the majority of LVO cases, and assessed the impact of EP2 inhibition on brain injury and inflammation. Finally, we examined the effects of EP2 inhibition in neuron-glia mixed cultures exposed to oxygen-glucose deprivation (OGD) without reoxygenation. After systemic administration in mice, new compounds exhibited favourable plasma half-lives and brain penetration. In the pMCAO model, treatment with EP2 antagonists significantly reduced brain infarction in both male and female mice, in a dose-dependent manner, whilst improving sensorimotor performance without affecting muscle strength. These benefits were accompanied by reduced neuronal death, lowered pro-inflammatory cytokines and attenuated reactive gliosis within the ischaemic penumbra. In addition, EP2 inhibition by CJ-18 conferred marked neuroprotection in neuron-glia co-cultures exposed to prolonged OGD, preserving neurite integrity and postsynaptic density. This proof-of-concept study supports our drug-like EP2 receptor antagonists, particularly CJ-18, as potential treatments for permanent focal cerebral ischaemia.

title: Role of Miro1 in Mitochondrial Dysfunction and Neurodegeneration in Huntington's Disease.
abstract: Huntington's Disease (HD) is an autosomal dominant neurodegenerative disorder that is caused by expansion of Cytosine-Adenine-Guanine (CAG) repeats in the Huntingtin (HTT) gene and leads to progressive motor, cognitive, and psychiatric dysfunction. Mitochondrial dysfunction is a major pathological feature of HD. Mitochondrial Rho GTPase 1 (Miro1) controls mitochondrial trafficking, calcium homeostasis, mitophagy, and neuronal signaling, and its dysregulation may contribute significantly to the progression of HD. The literature search to identify relevant studies on Miro1 biology, mitochondrial dysfunction, mitophagy, neuroinflammation, and emerging therapeutic strategies in HD followed a narrative review of the PubMed, Scopus, ScienceDirect, and Google Scholar databases. Original research articles, review articles, and preclinical studies published in English were screened for relevance, and the retrieved evidence was critically synthesized to provide an updated overview of Miro1's role in HD pathogenesis and its therapeutic potential. Mutant Huntingtin (mHTT) perturbs Miro1-dependent mitochondrial transport, which leads to mitochondrial mislocalization, defective mitophagy, oxidative stress, and synaptic dysfunction. Miro1 dysregulation also facilitates neuroinflammatory signaling and neuronal vulnerability. Advances in AI have led to improved early diagnosis of HD through neuroimaging and digital biomarkers. Emerging therapies targeting Miro1, including gene therapy, nanocarriers, and pharmacological modulators, show promising neuroprotective potential in preclinical models. Miro1 is a potentially important molecular link between mitochondrial dysfunction and neurodegeneration in HD. Targeting Miro1-mediated pathways may restore mitochondrial homeostasis and may be a promising therapeutic strategy for disease modification.

title: Neurovascular Modulation of the Blood-brain Barrier Using Focused Ultrasound for Antisense Therapy Delivery in Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis.
abstract: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a fatal neurodegenerative disease, and the blood-brain barrier (BBB) restricts CNS delivery of macromolecular therapeutics such as antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs). Focused ultrasound (FUS) with microbubbles enables transient, noninvasive opening of the BBB for deliver SOD1-targeted ASOs. A narrative review of the literature in PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar (2020-2025) was conducted to evaluate FUS-assisted delivery of SOD1-targeted ASOs, with an emphasis on lipid- and calcium phosphate (CaP)- based nanoparticles. Preclinical studies showed that FUS-mediated BBB opening (250 kHz; mechanical index 0.33; 30-s exposure; 0.15 mL/kg microbubbles) increased brain accumulation of nanoparticle- encapsulated ASOs by >3.5-fold compared with FUS without microbubbles. CaP lipid nanoparticles (~73 nm; -21 mV; 23-30% encapsulation efficiency) encapsulating tofersen demonstrated pH-responsive intracellular release. In wild-type and G93A SOD1 transgenic mice, FUS combined with CaP-ASO nanoparticles reduced SOD1 expression in sonicated cortical regions and increased lumbar spinal motor-neuron counts without detectable neuroinflammation or tissue damage. Combining FUS-mediated BBB modulation with CaP nanoparticles provides a minimally invasive strategy for CNS ASO delivery. Observed spinal cord effects suggest wider CNS distribution, potentially involving CSF transport and retrograde axonal pathways. Clinical translation requires optimising FUS parameters, conducting long-term safety assessments, and managing skull acoustic variability. MRI-guided FUS combined with CaP lipid nanoparticles represents a promising non-invasive platform for SOD1-targeted ASO delivery and precision gene therapy in ALS.

title: Medicinal Plants in the Management of Anxiety Disorders: Clinical Evidence, Mechanisms, and Safety Considerations.
abstract: Anxiety disorders are among the most prevalent neuropsychiatric conditions worldwide and represent a major public health burden. Although conventional pharmacological treatments are effective, their long-term use is often limited by adverse effects, including sedation, dependence, and cognitive impairment, prompting growing interest in medicinal plants as alternative or adjunct therapies. This review summarizes current evidence on selected medicinal plants, including Bacopa monnieri, Crocus sativus, Withania somnifera, and Piper methysticum, with emphasis on their pharmacological mechanisms, therapeutic efficacy, and safety profiles in anxiety management. Preclinical and clinical studies suggest that these plants exert anxiolytic effects through modulation of neurotransmitter systems, particularly γ-Aminobutyric Acid (GABA), serotonin, and dopamine pathways, as well as regulation of the Hypothalamic-Pituitary-Adrenal (HPA) axis. In addition, antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties may contribute to neuroprotection and improved stress resilience. Clinical findings indicate that certain herbal preparations may offer benefits comparable to conventional therapies for mild to moderate anxiety, often with fewer adverse effects. However, variability in study design, lack of standardized formulations, and insufficient long-term safety data remain significant limitations. Therefore, well-designed randomized controlled trials and mechanistic investigations are required to establish efficacy, safety, and standardization. Overall, medicinal plants show promising potential as complementary or alternative therapeutic options for anxiety disorders, provided their use is supported by rigorous scientific validation.

title: Overview of the Mechanistic Potential of Serotonin Reuptake Transporters in Depression.
abstract: Depression is considered to be one of the most common psychiatric disorders that affect millions of people, despite a large amount of unrecorded data. This disorder has been associated with feelings of hopelessness, sleep disturbances, and even suicidal thoughts. However, the serotonin hypothesis emerged in the 1960s, suggesting that serotonin was one of the key neurotransmitters associated with depression by regulating mood, emotion, and cognitive effects. The serotonin reuptake transporter (SERT) plays a vital role in maintaining homeostasis by facilitating the reuptake of synaptic serotonin into presynaptic neurons. The dysregulation of SERT has been potentially involved in the pathophysiology of depressive disorder and its related disorders. This manuscript provides an overview of the pharmacological aspects of SERT, including its mechanism of action, regulation, role in depression, and potential therapeutic targets. Current antidepressant research is increasingly focused on the development of highly selective and rapid-acting modulators of the SERT to overcome the delayed onset of action and limited efficacy associated with conventional selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs). Emerging strategies include designing allosteric SERT inhibitors that bind to alternative sites on the transporter, potentially enhancing selectivity while minimizing adverse effects. In parallel, the integration of pharmacogenomic insights into clinical practice seeks to personalize antidepressant therapy based on individual genetic variations-particularly polymorphisms in the SLC6A4 gene and related molecular markers-thereby improving therapeutic precision and overall treatment outcomes. Allosteric modulation of selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors and pharmacogenomics- guided treatment selection highlight the need to maximize therapeutic outcomes and fulfill the unmet needs of patients who suffer from depression.

title: Measurement of subjective cognitive decline and prediction of longitudinal clinical outcomes in older adults: a systematic review.
journal: Journal of clinical and experimental neuropsychology
abstract: Subjective cognitive decline (SCD) is a preclinical risk factor for Alzheimer's disease and may represent one of the earliest clinical indicators of underlying neurodegeneration. Prevalence estimates vary but suggest that between 20 and 30% of cognitively unimpaired older adults report some form of subjective decline (Rohr et al. 2020). Longitudinal studies indicate that individuals with SCD are at approximately twice the risk of progressing to mild cognitive impairment (MCI) or dementia compared to those without complaints. While not every older adult reporting decline will progress, early detection allows for timely intervention and risk stratification for clinical trials of dementia prevention. The current review examined longitudinal studies of adults aged ≥ 60 to assess and highlight the heterogeneity in operational definitions of SCD and risk of incident MCI or dementia. Among the 26 studies reviewed, 24 distinct definitions of SCD were used, highlighting the need for standardized measurement to improve comparability and generalizability. Of the studies reporting hazard ratios, all nine found that SCD was associated with a significantly higher risk of incident MCI or dementia compared to cognitively healthy older adults not reporting SCD; with the exception that no significant association between SCD and risk of vascular dementia was observed. The consistent association between SCD and risk of progression to MCI and dementia in these studies strengthens the evidence that suggests SCD may not be a benign complaint of aging or psychiatric conditions, but a potentially early clinical indicator of possible underlying neurodegenerative changes. These findings highlight the need for standardization in measurement tools and definitions to refine this pre-MCI construct.

title: Context-dependent TREM2 signalling in myeloid cells: Molecular mechanisms and immunotherapeutic divergence in neurodegeneration and cancer.
abstract: Triggering receptor expressed on myeloid cells 2 (TREM2) is a pivotal lipid-sensing receptor that governs the functional plasticity and metabolic fitness of mononuclear phagocytes, including microglia, osteoclasts, dendritic cells and tissue-resident macrophages.
